titles.why: A gentle, very funny bear adventure. It works just as well for adults.
A polite bear shakes up a London family. Sweet, clever, and quick.
Sword fights, true love, and endlessly quotable lines.
A grumpy weatherman relives the same day until he gets it right.
A twisty whodunit in a creepy mansion full of awful relatives.
The detective from Knives Out takes on a billionaire's island getaway.
Lush, swoony Jane Austen, with the most famous hand flex in film.
ABBA songs on a Greek island. Pure sunshine.
A storybook caper about a hotel concierge, a stolen painting, and a lot of pastry.
She meets his very rich, very judgmental family in Singapore.
Elle Woods proves everyone at Harvard Law wrong, in pink.
A broke rocker fakes his way into teaching fifth grade and forms a band.
A foster kid and a grumpy uncle go on the run in the New Zealand bush.
A burned-out chef starts over with a food truck and his son. You'll get hungry.
Can men and women just be friends? The romcom that set the rules.
Business rivals fall for each other over email. Cozy New York charm.
A London bookseller falls for the world's biggest movie star.
A widower's radio call-in sparks a cross-country almost-romance.
Two dreamers, one musical, and an ending people still argue about.
Four sisters, big ambitions, and a warm, lively retelling.
A meddling matchmaker in gorgeous pastel Regency England.
Emma Thompson's Austen: two sisters, heartbreak, and a very patient colonel.
Audrey Hepburn's runaway princess spends one perfect day in Rome.
Love and sacrifice in wartime Morocco. It's the classic for a reason.
Hollywood's switch to talkies, told through joyful song and dance.
Julie Andrews, the Alps, and songs you already know by heart.
A young Irish immigrant in 1950s New York is torn between two lives.
Childhood sweethearts reunite decades later. Quiet and aching.
A man who can time-travel learns what matters. It's a real tearjerker.
Two strangers walk and talk all night in Vienna.
Two musicians on the run hide in an all-woman band. Marilyn at her funniest.
A newly single dad gets dating lessons from a smooth-talking stranger.
The big, rain-soaked 1940s love story. Critics shrugged, audiences sobbed.
Two wedding guests get stuck in the same day, forever. Short and sharp.
A couples' murder-mystery night turns into a real kidnapping.
Maid-of-honor chaos, with Kristen Wiig and Melissa McCarthy at full power.
A laundromat owner fights across the multiverse. Wild, funny, and moving.
A linguist tries to talk to aliens, and the answer will floor you.
A space mission to save humanity, with a father-daughter story at its heart.
Stranded on Mars, an astronaut science-es his way home, with jokes.
A heist inside dreams, inside dreams. Keep your eyes on the screen.
The true story of how NASA got three astronauts home. It's nail-biting.
The Black women mathematicians who got America into space.
Jodie Foster picks up a signal from space. Big questions, big heart.
A lonely man falls for his AI assistant. Tender and eerily current.
A tense three-person chess game over whether a robot is conscious.
A desert planet, giant sandworms, and a young man's destiny. Epic scale.
The war for the desert planet explodes. Watch Part One first.
A teen in a time-traveling DeLorean has to get his parents together.
Dinosaurs, reborn. The T. rex scene still holds up.
Indiana Jones races Nazis to a legendary relic. The gold standard of adventure.
Real jets, real G-forces, and a big crowd-pleasing finish.
A two-hour desert car chase led by Charlize Theron. It's relentless.
Tom Cruise does his own stunts, including a helicopter chase.
One cop, one skyscraper, and a lot of bad guys.
Batman versus Heath Ledger's unforgettable Joker.
A betrayed Roman general fights his way back in the arena.

titles.t: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
titles.why: The epic quest begins. Settle in for a long, beautiful journey.
Swashbuckling 1920s Egypt adventure. Goofy, fun, and endlessly rewatchable.
Daniel Craig's first Bond: tough, stylish, and a high-stakes poker game.
Farm boy, princess, smuggler, and the Force. Where it all started.
A boy hides a lost alien. The bike scene still gives chills.
A lonely trash robot falls in love. Almost wordless and pure magic.
A widower ties balloons to his house and floats off. Have tissues ready.
A boy's musical journey through the Land of the Dead. Colorful and moving.
A girl is trapped in a bathhouse for spirits. Wondrous animation (English dub available).
Two sisters befriend a giant fluffy forest spirit. The ultimate calm-down movie.
A Brooklyn teen becomes Spider-Man. Dazzling, comic-book-style animation.
The feelings inside an 11-year-old's head. Smart about how emotions work.
A rat who dreams of cooking in Paris. Delicious.
Woody and Buzz, the rivalry that started Pixar. Short and perfect.
A worried clownfish dad crosses the ocean. Just keep swimming.
Hope and friendship behind prison walls. Audiences' favorite film for decades.
A kind man drifts through 30 years of American history.
A crime family, a reluctant heir, and an offer you can't refuse.
A janitor-genius and his therapist. It's not your fault.
Robin Williams teaches prep-school boys to seize the day.
A small-time boxer gets one shot at the title. Cue the steps.
A newly integrated 1971 football team learns to play as one.
Brad Pitt rebuilds a broke baseball team with math. It's a thrill even if you don't like sports.
The founding of Facebook as a razor-sharp betrayal story.
Boston Globe reporters dig into a massive cover-up. Gripping and important.
One juror holds out. A single room, and riveting the whole way.
A poor family cons its way into a rich household, then everything turns.
A shy Parisian secretly improves strangers' lives. Whimsical and warm.
A wealthy quadriplegic and his unlikely caregiver become best friends.
A father shields his son from the horror of a camp with imagination.
A teen con artist and the FBI agent chasing him. Breezy '60s fun.
Clooney, Pitt & co. rob three Vegas casinos at once. Effortlessly cool.
Newman and Redford pull off a 1930s long con. You'll be conned too.
The oddballs who saw the 2008 crash coming. Funny and furious.
The CIA smuggles hostages out of Iran with a fake movie. It's true.
The only hearing member of a Deaf family dreams of singing.
A broke single mom takes on a giant utility company, and wins.
A senior year of fights and love between a teen and her mom.
Meryl Streep as the fashion boss from hell. Deliciously watchable.
The WWII women's baseball league. There's no crying in baseball!
Barbie leaves Barbieland for the real world. Pink, funny, and sharper than expected.
A dysfunctional family road trip to a kids' pageant, in a broken VW bus.
Salieri's jealousy of the giggling genius Mozart. Glorious music.
A grumpy teacher, a stranded student, and a grieving cook over a 1970 Christmas break.
The man who built the atomic bomb. Three hours that fly by.
A stammering king and his unconventional speech therapist.
Two soldiers race across WWI no-man's-land, filmed as one continuous shot.
After D-Day, a squad searches for one soldier. Intense and unforgettable.
Ford's underdogs try to beat Ferrari at Le Mans. Thrilling racing.
Jack, Rose, and the unsinkable ship. The ultimate epic romance.
Meryl Streep as Julia Child, and a blogger cooking all her recipes.
You're gonna need a bigger boat. The original summer blockbuster.
A wrongly convicted doctor runs, and Tommy Lee Jones chases.

titles.t: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
titles.why: Johnny Depp's wobbly Captain Jack and cursed pirates. Swashbuckling fun.
Tom Cruise dies, wakes up, and repeats until he wins the alien war.
What if reality is fake? Red pill, blue pill, bullet time.
A slow, stunning noir about what makes us human. Best on a big screen.
Sandra Bullock, adrift in space. Ninety breathless minutes.
A British warship hunts a French frigate in 1805. Salty and rousing.
The WWII evacuation from land, sea, and air. A ticking clock the whole way.
Lincoln's fight to pass the 13th Amendment. Daniel Day-Lewis is uncanny.
A pianist and his bouncer-driver tour the 1962 Deep South.
Black maids in 1960s Mississippi tell their stories. It's a book club favorite.
A wisecracking pregnant teen picks adoptive parents. Funny and tender.
A widow lives on the road in her van across the American West.
A Korean family starts a farm in 1980s Arkansas, with a wonderful grandma.
One day, a man's best friend just stops talking to him. Darkly funny.
Sherlock's clever teen sister solves her own case. Brisk and charming.
A boy with a facial difference starts fifth grade. Choose kind.
Two friends on the run in a convertible. An iconic road trip.
Robin Williams disguises himself as a nanny to see his kids.
Climbing El Capitan with no ropes. Your palms will sweat.
A diver befriends an octopus in a kelp forest. Calming and surprising.
The radical kindness of Mister Rogers. A balm for a rough day.
A forgotten musician was a secret superstar in South Africa. Amazing twist.
The moon landing in never-before-seen footage. No narrator needed.
Peter Jackson brings WWI footage to life in color, in the soldiers' own words.
An 85-year-old sushi master chasing perfection. Meditative.
Lost footage of a 1969 Harlem music festival: Stevie, Nina, Mahalia.
The 1974 high-wire walk between the Twin Towers, told like a heist.
Triplets separated at birth find each other, and a dark secret.
Ruth Bader Ginsburg, from pioneering lawyer to pop-culture icon.
An American football coach's relentless kindness wins over English soccer.
A rich family goes broke and moves to a tiny town. It gets sweeter every season.
Underfunded Philly teachers who care too much. It's warm and very funny.
Paper-company cringe and Jim-and-Pam romance. The king of comfort TV.
Leslie Knope's boundless optimism in small-town government. (Skip season 1!)
Goofy detectives who are secretly great at their jobs. Noice.
A selfish woman sneaks into heaven. A comedy about ethics with killer twists.
Steve Martin, Martin Short, and Selena Gomez host a true-crime podcast about their neighbors.
Messy, hilarious, heartbreaking. Just 12 episodes, and there's a Hot Priest.
Teen girls in 1990s Northern Ireland. Laugh-out-loud from minute one.
Six friends, one coffee shop, 236 episodes of comfort.
A show about nothing, and every episode is a classic.
Two snobby psychiatrist brothers and their down-to-earth dad. Farce perfection.
Four Miami roommates, cheesecake, and zingers. Thank you for being a friend.
The Boston bar where everybody knows your name.
Three branches of one chaotic family, mockumentary-style.
Kind people bake in a tent. It's the most soothing competition on TV.
A Vegas comedy legend and a Gen-Z writer who can't stand each other.
A fine-dining chef takes over his family's chaotic sandwich shop. Yes, chef.
A grieving therapist starts telling patients the blunt truth. Harrison Ford steals it.

titles.t: What We Do in the Shadows
titles.why: Clueless vampire roommates on Staten Island. Totally absurd.
British comedians do ridiculous tasks for a stern judge. Free on YouTube!
A joyful goofball eats his way around the world.
Five experts give someone a life makeover. You will cry happy tears.
A 1958 housewife becomes a stand-up comic. Snappy and colorful.
Army surgeons joke to survive the Korean War. Funny, and deeper than you remember.
Big-box store employees, workplace chaos, and a slow-burn romance.
Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin, starting over at 70 when their husbands fall for each other.
A Korean-Canadian family runs a Toronto corner store. Gentle, funny, and kind.
Two metal-detecting friends in the English countryside. The coziest show ever made.
A cartoon for kids that grown-ups secretly love. Seven minutes of pure joy.
A woman keeps dying at her own birthday party and restarting. Weird and wonderful.
Fashion, croissants, and romantic drama in Paris. Pure escapism.
Everyone in this trial is an actor, except one very nice juror.
A woman who can always tell when someone's lying solves a new case each week.
Aristocrats upstairs, servants downstairs, and the Dowager's one-liners.
Midwives and nuns in 1950s East London. Kind-hearted and a little weepy.
A brooding soldier returns to Cornwall's cliffs and mines. Sweeping romance.
A Victorian slow-burn romance in a mill town. Only four episodes, and fans adore it.
An imaginative orphan finds a home on Prince Edward Island.
Regency romance with gossip, gowns, and string-quartet pop songs.
Queen Elizabeth II's reign, told with lavish, prestige polish.
An orphan becomes a chess prodigy. Seven episodes, all gripping.
1960s ad men, secrets, and cocktails. Stylish and layered.
A chemistry teacher turns drug kingpin. Hard to stop once you start.
A small-time lawyer's slow slide into crime. Patient and brilliant.
Horrible rich siblings fight to inherit a media empire. Vicious and funny.
A New Jersey mob boss goes to therapy. The show that changed TV.
Families battle for the Iron Throne in an epic fantasy saga. Big commitment.
The true story of one WWII company, from D-Day to the war's end.
The 1986 nuclear disaster and its cover-up. Five chilling hours.
A smuggler escorts a teen across a ruined America. Surprisingly tender.
One ER shift, one hour per episode. Intense and deeply humane.
Kate Winslet as a weary small-town detective. Wooder, anyone?
Monterey moms, dark secrets, and a murder at trivia night.
Power, loyalty, and politics in 1600 Japan. Record-breaking Emmy haul.
Midwestern-nice crime stories gone very wrong. Each season stands alone.
Office workers have their work memories surgically split off. Eerie and addictive.
MI5's rejects, led by a gloriously gross Gary Oldman. Sharp spy fun.
Ten thousand people live in an underground silo. Why? Don't ask.
A 1950s chemist ends up hosting a TV cooking show and teaches science.
A reluctant ambassador juggles a global crisis and her messy marriage.
'80s kids on bikes versus monsters from another dimension.
Stand-alone episodes about technology gone wrong. Start with 'San Junipero.'
A lone bounty hunter and Baby Yoda. A space Western.
The grown-up Star Wars: how an ordinary thief becomes a rebel.
Captain Picard's crew explores space and solves problems by talking. Comfort sci-fi.
Classic optimistic Star Trek adventures, one new planet per episode.
Realistic space politics and a scrappy crew in a colonized solar system.
Benedict Cumberbatch's Sherlock in modern London. Each episode is movie-length.
A boy's death shakes a seaside town. Olivia Colman and David Tennant.
Clear eyes, full hearts. A Texas town and its football team. It's more about family than football.
One family across decades. Guaranteed tears, every episode.
A fast-talking mom and daughter, coffee, and a cozy Connecticut town.
Idealistic White House staff walk and talk fast. Deeply rewatchable.
Soviet spies posing as a suburban 1980s American couple.
A young vet in 1930s Yorkshire. Sheep, tea, and gentle kindness.
A 1920s Birmingham gang, sharp suits, and razor caps.
A WWII nurse falls through time into 1743 Scotland, and falls in love.
David Attenborough and jaw-dropping wildlife. The iguana-versus-snakes chase!
Stunning nature footage, narrated by Attenborough.
Each episode is a gorgeous portrait of one world-class chef.
Michael Jordan and the '90s Bulls. Riveting even for non-fans.
Behind the scenes of F1 racing. It's turned countless people into fans.
Travel, food, and real conversation with the late, great Bourdain.
Fly on the wall as the Beatles write an album. Watch 'Get Back' being born.
A community-college study group of misfits. Paintball episodes!
